The 18 documented 99215 claims all support the billed level, but heavy note duplication leaves open whether that documentation reflects the visits.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The billing pattern points toward upcoding: the 99215 share runs about double the all-provider share in every complexity band, including patients with 0–1 conditions, so case mix does not explain the excess, and the low-complexity sample includes visits such as rash (C0035146, C0035252) and URI (C0035630, C0036009) billed at 99215. Against that, none of the 18 documented 99215 claims fell below the billed level, and some low-complexity claims look supported (for example C0035959, heart failure, documented high MDM at 54 minutes), which fits a legitimately complex panel. That support is weakened by the note signals: over a third of returned notes appear duplicated, a smaller share repeat the same visit time, and no audit trail was received, so the supporting notes could be cloned rather than reflecting the actual visits. The data-reviewed-without-lab finding adds only weak evidence. A reviewer should first ask for the audit trail and compare the duplicated notes, starting with the problem-flagged 99215 claims C0035197 and C0035227, to see whether the high-MDM content is copied text. Records cover under 5% of claims, and the higher-than-peer unsupported rate on 99214 (C0035228, C0035556) is too thin to act on alone, so a larger targeted pull of low-complexity 99215 charts is the clearest next step."}
